NKJV.1: Remember, O LORD, what has come upon us; Look, and behold our reproach!
NKJV.2: Our inheritance has been turned over to aliens, And our houses to foreigners.
NKJV.3: We have become orphans and waifs, Our mothers are like widows.
NKJV.4: We pay for the water we drink, And our wood comes at a price.
NKJV.5: They pursue at our heels; We labor and have no rest.
NKJV.6: We have given our hand to the Egyptians And the Assyrians, to be satisfied with bread.
NKJV.7: Our fathers sinned and are no more, But we bear their iniquities.
NKJV.8: Servants rule over us; There is none to deliver us from their hand.
NKJV.9: We get our bread at the risk of our lives, Because of the sword in the wilderness.
NKJV.10: Our skin is hot as an oven, Because of the fever of famine.
NKJV.11: They ravished the women in Zion, The maidens in the cities of Judah.
NKJV.12: Princes were hung up by their hands, And elders were not respected.
NKJV.13: Young men ground at the millstones; Boys staggered under loads of wood.
NKJV.14: The elders have ceased gathering at the gate, And the young men from their music.
NKJV.15: The joy of our heart has ceased; Our dance has turned into mourning.
NKJV.16: The crown has fallen from our head. Woe to us, for we have sinned!
NKJV.17: Because of this our heart is faint; Because of these things our eyes grow dim;
NKJV.18: Because of Mount Zion which is desolate, With foxes walking about on it.
NKJV.19: You, O LORD, remain forever;  Your throne from generation to generation.
NKJV.20: Why do You forget us forever, And forsake us for so long a time?
NKJV.21: Turn us back to You, O LORD, and we will be restored; Renew our days as of old,
NKJV.22: Unless You have utterly rejected us, And are very angry with us!

ESV.1: Remember, O LORD, what has befallen us; look, and see our disgrace!
ESV.2: Our inheritance has been turned over to strangers, our homes to foreigners.
ESV.3: We have become orphans, fatherless; our mothers are like widows.
ESV.4: We must pay for the water we drink; the wood we get must be bought.
ESV.5: Our pursuers are at our necks; we are weary; we are given no rest.
ESV.6: We have given the hand to Egypt, and to Assyria, to get bread enough.
ESV.7: Our fathers sinned, and are no more; and we bear their iniquities.
ESV.8: Slaves rule over us; there is none to deliver us from their hand.
ESV.9: We get our bread at the peril of our lives, because of the sword in the wilderness.
ESV.10: Our skin is hot as an oven with the burning heat of famine.
ESV.11: Women are raped in Zion, young women in the towns of Judah.
ESV.12: Princes are hung up by their hands; no respect is shown to the elders.
ESV.13: Young men are compelled to grind at the mill, and boys stagger under loads of wood.
ESV.14: The old men have left the city gate, the young men their music.
ESV.15: The joy of our hearts has ceased; our dancing has been turned to mourning.
ESV.16: The crown has fallen from our head; woe to us, for we have sinned!
ESV.17: For this our heart has become sick, for these things our eyes have grown dim,
ESV.18: for Mount Zion which lies desolate; jackals prowl over it.
ESV.19: But you, O LORD, reign forever; your throne endures to all generations.
ESV.20: Why do you forget us forever, why do you forsake us for so many days?
ESV.21: Restore us to yourself, O LORD, that we may be restored! Renew our days as of old —
ESV.22: unless you have utterly rejected us, and you remain exceedingly angry with us.

NLT.1:
LORD, remember what has happened to us.
See how we have been disgraced!
NLT.2:
Our inheritance has been turned over to strangers,
our homes to foreigners.
NLT.3:
We are orphaned and fatherless.
Our mothers are widowed.
NLT.4:
We have to pay for water to drink,
and even firewood is expensive.
NLT.5:
Those who pursue us are at our heels;
we are exhausted but are given no rest.
NLT.6:
We submitted to Egypt and Assyria
to get enough food to survive.
NLT.7:
Our ancestors sinned, but they have died —
and we are suffering the punishment they deserved!
NLT.8:
Slaves have now become our masters;
there is no one left to rescue us.
NLT.9:
We hunt for food at the risk of our lives,
for violence rules the countryside.
NLT.10:
The famine has blackened our skin
as though baked in an oven.
NLT.11:
Our enemies rape the women in Jerusalem
and the young girls in all the towns of Judah.
NLT.12:
Our princes are being hanged by their thumbs,
and our elders are treated with contempt.
NLT.13:
Young men are led away to work at millstones,
and boys stagger under heavy loads of wood.
NLT.14:
The elders no longer sit in the city gates;
the young men no longer dance and sing.
NLT.15:
Joy has left our hearts;
our dancing has turned to mourning.
NLT.16:
The garlands have fallen from our heads.
Weep for us because we have sinned.
NLT.17:
Our hearts are sick and weary,
and our eyes grow dim with tears.
NLT.18:
For Jerusalem is empty and desolate,
a place haunted by jackals.
NLT.19:
But LORD, you remain the same forever!
Your throne continues from generation to generation.
NLT.20:
Why do you continue to forget us?
Why have you abandoned us for so long?
NLT.21:
Restore us, O LORD, and bring us back to you again!
Give us back the joys we once had!
NLT.22:
Or have you utterly rejected us?
Are you angry with us still?

MSG.1:
"Remember, God, all we've been through.
Study our plight, the black mark we've made in history.
MSG.2:
Our precious land has been given to outsiders,
our homes to strangers.
MSG.3:
Orphans we are, not a father in sight,
and our mothers no better than widows.
MSG.4:
We have to pay to drink our own water.
Even our firewood comes at a price.
MSG.5:
We're nothing but slaves, bullied and bowed,
worn out and without any rest.
MSG.6:
We sold ourselves to Assyria and Egypt
just to get something to eat.
MSG.7:
Our parents sinned and are no more,
and now we're paying for the wrongs they did.
MSG.8:
Slaves rule over us;
there's no escape from their grip.
MSG.9:
We risk our lives to gather food
in the bandit-infested desert.
MSG.10:
Our skin has turned black as an oven,
dried out like old leather from the famine.
MSG.11:
Our wives were raped in the streets in Zion,
and our virgins in the cities of Judah.
MSG.12:
They hanged our princes by their hands,
dishonored our elders.
MSG.13:
Strapping young men were put to women's work,
mere boys forced to do men's work.
MSG.14:
The city gate is empty of wise elders.
Music from the young is heard no more.
MSG.15:
All the joy is gone from our hearts.
Our dances have turned into dirges.
MSG.16:
The crown of glory has toppled from our head.
Woe! Woe! Would that we'd never sinned!
MSG.17:
Because of all this we're heartsick;
we can't see through the tears.
MSG.18:
On Mount Zion, wrecked and ruined,
jackals pace and prowl.
MSG.19:
And yet, God, you're sovereign still,
your throne intact and eternal.
MSG.20:
So why do you keep forgetting us?
Why dump us and leave us like this?
MSG.21:
Bring us back to you, God—we're ready to come back.
Give us a fresh start.
MSG.22:
As it is, you've cruelly disowned us.
You've been so very angry with us."

NET.22: unless you have utterly rejected us and are angry with us beyond measure.
